assumptions.original: The positive horizon is T. The sample measure is finite, the filtration satisfies the usual conditions, and the driving standard vector Brownian motion is relative to that filtration and measure. The finite coordinate rows have progressive product-square-integrable diffusion coefficients. Their drift evaluations at each fixed time t≤T are almost-everywhere strongly measurable. Almost every drift path is continuous with bounded variation on [0,T]. The compact set K has a selected fallback point k₀. On one event of full measure, the process belongs to K at every time in [0,T]. The test is twice continuously Fréchet differentiable at each point of K.
assumptions.reconstructed: B starts at zero for every omega, has jointly independent increments over disjoint half-open intervals, every continuous real linear functional ell sends B_t-B_s (s<t) to a centered Gaussian of variance (t-s)||ell||², and paths are continuous mu-a.e. B is strongly adapted to F and B_t-B_s is independent of F_s for s≤t. F is right-continuous and every subset S⊆Omega with mu(S)=0 belongs to F_t for every t≥0. A progressive L² integrand is a real process a(t,omega), strongly progressive for F, for which (omega,t)↦a(t,omega) is in L²(mu⊗lambda_T). For every i and t≤T, A_i(t,·) is mu-a.e. strongly measurable. For every i, mu-a.e. omega, A_i(·,omega) is continuous and of bounded variation on [0,T]. K compact, fallback∈K; f is ambient C² at every point of K. On one mu-full set, X(t,omega)∈K for every t≤T. No progressivity of A_i is explicitly assumed.
assumptions.evidence: Full-module binder and definition audit: hAmeas and hA are exactly the weak marginal/path hypotheses. hWm uses the measurable fallback to avoid global derivative measurability, hLim applies weighted covariation, and hInt justifies the finite sum inside the time integral.

conclusion.original: Construct a Euclidean process from completed Itô rows. Suppose it stays in compact K almost surely throughout the horizon and the scalar test is twice continuously Fréchet differentiable at every point of K. The dyadic sum of half the Hessian applied twice to the actual increment converges in measure to the time integral of half the sum of the Hessian on the diffusion columns. Formula: \sum_i \tfrac12 D^2 f(X_{t_i})[\Delta_iX,\Delta_iX]\xrightarrow{\mu}\int_{[0,T]}\tfrac12\sum_j D^2f(X_s)[\sigma_j(s),\sigma_j(s)]\,ds.
conclusion.reconstructed: I_j(a)(t,omega) denotes the specified completed Ito integral driven by the scalar coordinate B^j(t,omega)=(B(t,omega))_j. Its representative is the pointwise limit of chosen elementary stochastic integrals off the null complement of their uniform Cauchy event, and zero on that complement; it is held constant after T. Define X_i(t)=A_i(t)+∑_j I_j(eta_ij)(t), t_r^n=rT/2^n, Delta_r^n X=X(t_{r+1}^n)-X(t_r^n). With H=D(Df) and sigma_j(s)=(eta_ij(s))_i, the functions (1/2)∑_{r=0}^{2^n-1}H(X(t_r^n))[Delta_r^n X,Delta_r^n X] converge in mu-measure to ∫(1/2)∑_j H(X(s))[sigma_j(s),sigma_j(s)]d lambda_T(s).
